# The signing surface of the Windows installer, as measured.
#
# Every line is a file that `installtest-windows.ps1 -SacAudit` saw Windows
# audit under Microsoft's SmartAppControlAuditNoISG policy -- i.e. a file that
# is NOT signed by a certificate Windows trusts, and that Smart App Control
# would block in enforcement mode. The key is <bucket>/<file name>, because the
# installer's working directories carry per-run randomness and a full path
# cannot be a stable ledger key.
#
# The harness asserts SET EQUALITY against this list, in both directions:
#
#   * a line that stops being audited means that file got signed. That must
#     fail here, so the list is shortened deliberately rather than drifting.
#   * a file audited but absent here is a binary that reached shipping without
#     anyone deciding whether it needs a signature.
#
# So on the day Windows signing lands (waired#759 Phase 0), this file is the
# checklist, and the leg names whichever artifact was missed.
#
# HOW TO FILL IT: run the mode once
#   gh workflow run installtest-inference.yml --ref <branch> -f os=windows
# and copy the keys the leg prints under "SacAudit: reading the CodeIntegrity
# audit ledger". An EMPTY list is a hard failure, on purpose: it cannot tell
# "nothing to sign" apart from "the audit never saw us".
#
# NOT MEASURED YET -- see the PR that introduced this file.
